title: The Power Reckoning
thesis_lead: Between August and October 2026 the scarce input for AI data centers stopped being megawatts alone and became permission: permission to connect, to co-locate and to build. Buyers reached for existing nuclear plants, while FERC, PJM and state officials in Texas, North Carolina and Virginia began rewriting who pays and who waits.
summary_heading: Permission has joined power as the constraint
thesis: The record in this Briefing is thirty-seven sourced items, Faraday Signals and crawled articles, dated between 13 August and 12 October 2026. Read together, they show two movements happening at once.

The first is a rush to existing nuclear capacity. Google signed a 20-year agreement with Constellation for 890 MW from upgrades at 11 existing units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey [1], with Constellation investing over $4.3 billion [2]. Amazon signed a 20-year agreement around Calvert Cliffs in Maryland [5]. Meta secured up to 6.6 GW from TerraPower, Oklo and Vistra [7]. The Department of Energy is lending into the same plants: a conditional $4.2 billion package for Vistra uprates adding 433 MW [6] and a closed $1.9 billion loan to restart Duane Arnold in Iowa [9].

The second is a tightening of the rules for connecting large loads. FERC issued show-cause orders in June 2026 to six grid operators over interconnection rules for loads above 50 MW [18]. PJM filed a mechanism that would require new large data center loads to bring qualifying capacity or face backstop procurement [19]. Texas paused new data center permits pending an ERCOT audit [28, 29]. North Carolina regulators refused a Duke Energy gas turbine request on cost and uncertain need [30].

Where those two movements meet, projects slip. Oracle invoked force majeure with STACK Infrastructure over delays at Project Jupiter, citing power supply, air permits and land access [13], and the 2.45 GW Bloom Energy fuel cell deployment tied to that site faces fuel supply delays [14]. The same report that tallied 9.8 GW of hyperscaler nuclear deals projected only 1 GW online before 2030 [12].

sections.name: Nuclear & SMR Offtake
sections.intro: Hyperscalers bought existing nuclear output and uprates in September and October, and federal lending followed the same plants. Every figure below is as reported by the cited source.

items.head: Google and Constellation add 890 MW to PJM
items.text: Google and Constellation Energy signed a 20-year power purchase agreement to add 890 MW of nuclear capacity to the PJM grid through upgrades at 11 existing nuclear units across Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey [1].

items.head: Constellation's side of the Google deal
items.text: Google committed to a 20-year agreement to secure 890 MW of nuclear power for its AI data centers, with Constellation investing over $4.3 billion in the partnership [2].

items.head: Uprates as the fastest path to new megawatts
items.text: Google, Meta and the Department of Energy are backing over 1.3 GW of reactor uprate deals through Constellation and Vistra, primarily targeting PJM capacity [3].

items.head: Uprates and the federal 5 GW goal
items.text: Constellation framed its uprate plans as supporting the administration's goal of adding 5 GW of carbon-free nuclear capacity by 2029 [4].

items.head: Amazon backs Calvert Cliffs
items.text: Amazon and Constellation signed a 20-year agreement supporting expansion and renovation at Maryland's 1,790 MW Calvert Cliffs plant [5].

items.head: DOE lines up $4.2 billion for Vistra
items.text: DOE's Energy Dominance Financing office announced a conditional $4.2 billion loan commitment for uprates and modernization at Beaver Valley (PA), Davis-Besse and Perry (OH), adding 433 MW [6].

items.head: Meta secures up to 6.6 GW
items.text: Meta secured up to 6.6 GW of nuclear power through agreements with TerraPower, Oklo and Vistra [7].

items.head: A running tally of data center nuclear deals
items.text: The tracker reports nuclear capacity agreements for data centers have grown to 45 GW [8].

items.head: Duane Arnold restart financed
items.text: DOE closed a $1.9 billion loan to NextEra Energy to restart the Duane Arnold plant in Iowa [9].

items.head: NRC timeline for Duane Arnold
items.text: The NRC is conducting 2026 site inspections ahead of a potential restart, with a licensing package expected by January 2028 [10].

items.head: X-energy's federal windfall
items.text: X-energy received $1 billion in DOE funding for advanced small modular reactor development [11].

items.head: Georgia Power subscription for uprates
items.text: Google partnered with Georgia Power to finance capacity uprates at nuclear facilities through a subscription program [36].

items.head: The gap between deals and delivery
items.text: Hyperscalers have announced 9.8 GW of nuclear deals, but only 1 GW is projected online before 2030, a 6 GW shortfall in PJM [12].

sections.name: Behind-the-Fence Gas & Fuel Cells
sections.intro: On-site generation is the main alternative to waiting for the grid. The record shows it carries its own permitting and fuel risks.

items.head: Oracle invokes force majeure at Project Jupiter
items.text: Oracle invoked force majeure with Blue Owl's STACK Infrastructure over Project Jupiter delays, citing power supply, air permits and land access [13].

items.head: Bloom's largest deployment at risk
items.text: Bloom Energy's 2.45 GW solid oxide fuel cell deployment at Project Jupiter in New Mexico faces fuel supply delays, putting its largest contracted project at risk [14].

items.head: Nebius picks fuel cells for New Jersey
items.text: Nebius endorsed Bloom Energy fuel cells for a planned 300 MW AI data center in Vineland, New Jersey, citing faster deployment and less community opposition than gas turbines [15].

items.head: A generator-to-chip delivery model
items.text: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launched a coordinated approach integrating onsite generation, electrical infrastructure and engineering [16].

items.head: A 20-year gas PPA in the Permian
items.text: New Era signed a 20-year agreement with a Vistra subsidiary for 250 MW of gas-fired power for a data center in Ector County, Texas [17].

sections.name: Large-Load Tariff Design & Co-Location Rules
sections.intro: The rules for plugging a data center into a wholesale market are being rewritten through FERC dockets and RTO filings. The Susquehanna case is the reference point.

items.head: FERC orders six operators to revise rules
items.text: FERC issued June 2026 show-cause orders to six grid operators requiring revised interconnection rules for loads above 50 MW, covering behind-the-meter generation, co-location and cost allocation [18].

items.head: PJM: bring power or face cuts
items.text: PJM filed a tariff revision proposing a 'Bring Your Own New Capacity' mechanism requiring new large data center loads to supply qualifying capacity or face reliability backstop procurement [19].

items.head: The Talen–Amazon order
items.text: FERC rejected Talen–Amazon's behind-the-meter arrangement at Susquehanna in November 2024, forcing a front-of-the-meter model by spring 2026 in which Talen supplies AWS via the PJM grid. The order directs PJM to create explicit transmission services for co-located loads [20].

items.head: Susquehanna goes front-of-meter
items.text: Amazon's Susquehanna campus transitioned to a front-of-the-meter configuration in spring 2026 after the regulatory proceedings concluded [21].

items.head: California argues over 'large load'
items.text: CAISO and PG&E are in dispute over the definition of 'large loads' as AI data centers seek grid access in California [22].

sections.name: Transmission, Reliability & Flexible Load
sections.intro: Federal reliability bodies moved data center flexibility from a voluntary practice toward a standard, and industry formed groups to supply it.

items.head: NERC alert, then a FERC mandate
items.text: NERC issued a Level 3 Alert on computational loads in May 2026, and FERC then directed NERC to develop computational-load reliability standards by year-end [23].

items.head: An alliance for flexible data centers
items.text: Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI launched the AI Energy Management Alliance to promote data centers that can cut power draw during grid strain [24].

items.head: Nvidia qualifies three battery suppliers
items.text: Nvidia launched a battery energy storage qualification program for AI data centers, initially naming Tesla, LG and Hitachi [25].

items.head: More capacity from existing lines
items.text: The Department of Energy launched a project to increase capacity on existing power lines to support data center demand [26].

items.head: Solar growth follows load in ERCOT and MISO
items.text: U.S. solar generation is projected to accelerate through 2027, driven primarily by data center demand in ERCOT and MISO [27].

sections.name: States, Moratoria & Utility Commissions
sections.intro: State actors moved faster than federal ones. Texas paused permits, North Carolina refused new gas, and Virginia's largest utility merger became a test of who speaks for ratepayers.

items.head: Texas halts new permits
items.text: Governor Greg Abbott halted new data center permits pending completion of an ERCOT audit of grid capacity and reliability [28].

items.head: Two agencies, one pause
items.text: The pause combines the governor's 3 August ERCOT audit directive with a 21 September TCEQ freeze on new data center permitting until the audit is complete [29].

items.head: North Carolina rejects Duke turbines
items.text: Regulators rejected Duke Energy's request for a gas turbine facility, citing staggering cost and uncertain need [30].

items.head: Arkansas ratepayers question Google–Entergy terms
items.text: Google's 'Fair Share Plus' arrangement with Entergy for a $4 billion West Memphis facility drew ratepayer concerns over redacted filings and trade-secret claims [31].

items.head: Kentucky doubles TeraWulf's power
items.text: TeraWulf doubled contracted power at its Muskie campus from 500 MW to 1 GW under an amended agreement with Kentucky Power, pulling the second phase from 2030 to 2029 [32].

items.head: Reset the clock on Dominion–NextEra
items.text: Attorney General Jay Jones asked the State Corporation Commission to reset the 180-day review of the $67 billion merger after the companies filed supplemental documents [33]. Legislators later said the window had closed to call a special session to extend the review [34].

items.head: Pennsylvania groups seek a moratorium
items.text: Environmental and community groups called on Governor Shapiro and lawmakers to pass a data center moratorium [35].

items.head: Amazon pledges $1 billion to host communities
items.text: Amazon pledged $1 billion to host communities as Washington Governor Bob Ferguson rolled back state tax breaks; Microsoft has sworn off seeking local subsidies [37].

take: The cited record does not show a shortage of buyers or of capital: in eight weeks it logs agreements covering several gigawatts of existing and uprated nuclear output [1, 5, 7] and billions in federal loans [6, 9]. What it shows instead is a queue of permissions, at FERC [18], in PJM [19], in Texas [28] and in state commissions [30, 33], each deciding who pays to connect large loads. On this evidence, the projects that slip will be the ones that waited for those decisions, as Project Jupiter shows [13]. The ones that hold their schedules will be the ones that bought capacity already on the grid.
method: Source rule: every factual sentence carries a numbered citation to a Faraday Signal (Supabase public.signals) or crawled artifact (public.artifacts); each records the publisher URL below. Sentences restate the recorded framing, using only its complete clauses where the record was truncated. Nothing comes from the retired Gamma deck or from model memory.

Selection: Signals tagged D2.5, D2.6, D2.8, D3.1–D3.5, fired 31 Jul–13 Oct 2026, de-duplicated by headline, Google News redirects excluded, then curated by hand. Mis-tagged Signals were dropped, and one report that described the Google–Constellation deal differently was excluded rather than reconciled.
Limits: primary articles were not re-fetched for this sample. Faraday's Take is analysis of the cited items and adds no facts. Status: draft, not signed off (Brand Bible §07).
